18   has evolved over the years and continues to this

22   opportunities for small businesses, for making

18                "WHEREAS, It is the sense of this 

19   Legislative Body to recognize and pay tribute to 

20   those singular individuals who devote their 

21   purposeful lives and careers in service to 

22   preserving the rights and protecting the welfare  

23   of the citizens of their community and the State 

24   of New York; and 

25                "WHEREAS, It is with feelings of 


                                                                118

 1   deepest regret that this Legislative Body records 

 2   the passing of Judith Kaye, noting the 

 3   significance of the loss of a woman whose 

 4   passionate and altruistic spirit will be greatly 

 5   missed; and 

 6                "WHEREAS, Judith S. Kaye, the first 

 7   female Chief Judge of the New York State Court of 

 8   Appeals, died on Thursday, January 7, 2016, at 

 9   the age of 77; and 

10                "WHEREAS, Born on August 4, 1938, in  

11   Monticello, New York, Judith Smith Kaye earned a 

12   bachelor's degree from Barnard College in 1958, 

13   before obtaining an LL.B. from New York 

14   University School of Law, cum laude, in 1962; one 

15   year later, she was admitted to the New York 

16   State Bar; and 

17                "WHEREAS, Judith S. Kaye began her 

18   eminent career in private practice in New York 

19   City with the firm of Sullivan & Cromwell; she 

20   then moved to Olwine, Connelly, Chase, O'Donnell 

21   & Weyher, until her historic appointment by 

22   Governor Mario Cuomo to the New York State Court 

23   of Appeals on March 23, 1993, the position she 

24   would hold until December 31, 2008, after 

25   becoming the first woman to be appointed Chief 


                                                                119

 1   Judge of the State's highest court; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, A legal scholar with a 

 3   keen mind whose visionary, thoughtful prose and, 

 4   above all, unfaltering belief in restorative 

 5   justice and fairness, throughout her 15 years as 

 6   New York State's Chief Judge resulted in a period 

 7   of unprecedented reform in the administration of 

 8   New York's Courts; she will be remembered for 

 9   writing several notable decisions on a wide 

10   variety of statutory, constitutional, and common 

11   law issues; and 

12                "WHEREAS, Her commitment to 

13   strengthening New York's child welfare system and 

14   her steadfast belief in the importance of family 

15   preservation helped to improve the lives of 

16   countless people across the state; and 

17                "WHEREAS, In recognition of Judith 

18   S. Kaye's outstanding intellect and impeccable 

19   work ethic, she was the recipient of the 1997 

20   Edith I. Spivack Award from the New York County  

21   Lawyers' Association's Women's Rights Committee; 

22   and 

23                "WHEREAS, Under Judith S. Kaye's  

24   leadership, New York State was considered a 

25   national leader in court reform efforts and in 


                                                                120

 1   establishing problem-solving courts; working with 

 2   the Fund for the City of New York, she helped 

 3   establish the Center for Court Innovation, a 

 4   nonprofit think tank that, although independent

 6   research and development arm; and

 8   Kaye also served as co-chair of the Commission on 

 9   the American Jury of the American Bar Association 

10   from 2004-2005; chair of the Permanent Judicial  

11   Commission on Justice for children; founding 

12   member and honorary chair of Judges and Lawyers 

13   Breast Cancer Alert (JALBCA); member of the Board 

14   of Editors, New York State Bar Journal; and 

15   trustee of the William Nelson Cromwell 

16   Foundation; and

18   S. Kaye retired, as state law requires, but this

20   appointed to the Commission on Judicial 

21   Nomination, which recommends finalists to the 

22   governor for positions on the Court of Appeals,
